experiments.label: Single-node · Inserts
experiments.note: Attempted insert throughput includes key generation. Failure counts were not exported for these pure-insert runs. Structure endpoints are PostgreSQL-only, at 1M and 10M.

experiments.label: Single-node · Point lookups
experiments.note: PostgreSQL draws random keys; MySQL fetches a limited unordered list, MongoDB natural-order IDs, Cassandra the smallest clustering keys. Identifier fetching is outside the timed loop but inside the broader I/O window where applicable. Compare within each engine.

experiments.label: Single-node · Updates
experiments.note: Attempted-operation throughput. The insert ranking need not carry over to updates. Target selection differs between engines as in the historical read workloads.

experiments.label: Single-node · Read / update mix
experiments.note: 50% read / 50% update selection probabilities; 200K requested operations. Attempted-operation throughput. The archived CSV RecordCount=1M is command-line metadata, NOT the 500K preload target.

experiments.label: Single-node · Insert-heavy (corrected)
experiments.sampler: Uniform sampling from all preload IDs
experiments.note: 70% insert / 30% read selection probabilities; 200K completed successful operations. Fixed pool of 100K preload IDs; new inserts never enter the pool. 125 selected runs: 122 originals + 3 documented replacements. No historical IH measurements or baselines are mixed in.

experiments.label: A5 · Inserts · 4 GB · 3 nodes
experiments.note: The load is the measured insert phase: eight concurrent writers, attempted rows/s. Small batch losses are recorded (at most 3,800 / 50M rows). Repeated 1 KiB payload; table sizes are cluster sums and cannot be read as a general storage-overhead percentage.

experiments.label: A1 · Reads · 4 GB · 3 nodes
experiments.note: Reads follow loading without waiting for compaction; one synchronous client; cgroup counters include background work. HDD storage, not SSD. All UUIDv4 throughput runs fall below all UUIDv7 runs. This does not identify a causal mechanism.

experiments.label: A2 · Reads · 32 GB · 3 nodes
experiments.note: Reads follow loading without waiting for compaction; one synchronous client; cgroup counters include background work. HDD storage, not SSD. Container memory, heap and new generation all change together. Read I/O is near zero. I/O-per-lookup is excluded: arm-wide median read I/O is 1.62 block ops/s (>1), and the median per-run write/read ratio is 70.19% (>5%). No significant throughput difference is NOT evidence of equivalence.

experiments.label: A3 · Reads · 4 GB · 1 node
experiments.note: Reads follow loading without waiting for compaction; one synchronous client; cgroup counters include background work. HDD storage, not SSD. Node count AND replication factor differ from A1 (1/RF1 versus 3/RF3); this is not an isolated node-count effect.

experiments.label: A4 · Reads · 4 GB · 3 nodes · head sampler
experiments.note: Reads follow loading without waiting for compaction; one synchronous client; cgroup counters include background work. HDD storage, not SSD. Method check only, n=3: the two smallest clustering keys per partition are fetched and read in returned order. This changes both target selection and order; fetching falls inside the I/O window.

throughput.label: Throughput
throughput.note: Throughput counts attempted operations in historical workloads and A1–A5; corrected IH counts completed successful operations. A1–A4 recorded no driver errors, but some lookups returned no row. LOCAL_ONE does not guarantee read-after-write consistency with RF3. Inserts include identifier generation.

p50_latency_us.label: Latency · p50
p50_latency_us.note: Per-run median operation latency. The chart shows the distribution of these per-run percentiles, not a pooled latency distribution.

p95_latency_us.label: Latency · p95
p95_latency_us.note: Per-run 95th-percentile operation latency; not the 95th percentile of the plotted run values.

p99_latency_us.label: Latency · p99
p99_latency_us.note: Per-run 99th-percentile operation latency. A2 runs occupy two latency ranges; these are descriptive observations, not evidence of a mechanism.

read_iops.label: Block-read rate
read_iops.note: cgroup v2 process-window rate, including setup and background activity, not just the timed query loop. Exported historical zeroes are limited by two-decimal precision.

write_iops.label: Block-write rate
write_iops.note: cgroup v2 process-window rate. During reads this includes concurrent background work. Insert-side counters are read when the workload returns: later flushes and compactions are omitted, under-counting insert-side writes by an unknown amount.

io_per_op.label: Block I/O per lookup
io_per_op.note: Per-run read_iops / read_throughput, following the paper protocol. Different measurement windows: not an isolated disk-access count per query. Excluded when both the arm-wide median read I/O exceeds 1 block operation/s and the median per-run write/read I/O ratio exceeds 5%. A2 meets both conditions; A4 is not offered.

table_size_mb.label: Table size
table_size_mb.note: Observed Cassandra live table size, summed across all nodes. Every row reuses the same 1 KiB payload. Percent differences are specific to these highly compressible data; not a pure key-byte cost.

index_size_mb.label: Index size
index_size_mb.note: PostgreSQL primary-index size after loading. The historical field ends in _mb but contains MiB.

page_splits.label: B-tree split records
page_splits.note: PostgreSQL instance-wide WAL B-tree split records around the insert workload. Split counts are not interchangeable with page occupancy or fragmentation.

avg_leaf_density.label: Leaf density
avg_leaf_density.note: Occupied percentage of usable PostgreSQL primary-index leaf-page space after loading.

fragmentation.label: Leaf fragmentation
fragmentation.note: PostgreSQL pgstatindex physical leaf-page ordering metric. Not percentage wasted space and not comparable to other engines’ fragmentation proxies.

sstable_count.label: SSTables at read start
sstable_count.note: Cassandra SSTable snapshot at read start, summed across nodes. Count alone does not identify range overlap or read amplification.

bloom_filter_fp.label: Bloom false-positive delta
bloom_filter_fp.note: Counter change clamped to zero per node, then summed. Compaction can mask increases. Zero does not mean no filter was consulted. Filters test partitions, not individual clustering keys; this is descriptive, not a mechanism test.
